title: Numbers and prices
description: Count from 0 to 100 in French, including the tricky 70, 80 and 90, and understand and say prices in euros on a visit to Provence.

sources.title: Nombres en français (Wikipédia)
sources.note: France: soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix; Belgium and Switzerland: septante, nonante; huitante in Vaud, Valais and Fribourg; et only in 21, 31 … 71 (not in 81, 91); quatre-vingts takes s only when no number follows; the 1990 spelling hyphenates every part (vingt-et-un).

sources.title: Euro (Wikipédia)
sources.note: In France the cent is called centime; the word cent is avoided because it is confusing.

sources.title: Séparateur décimal (Wikipédia)
sources.note: French uses the decimal comma (standard NF X 02-003); thousands are grouped with a space.

sources.title: Telephone numbers in France (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Ten digits, usually stated as five pairs (0x xx xx xx xx); 06 and 07 are mobile numbers.

sources.title: Liaison (French) (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Liaison between a number and the noun that follows (deux‿euros, six‿euros).

sources.title: French phonology (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Nasal vowels; the final stressed syllable of a phrase.

sources.title: ITER Organization: Visiting ITER
sources.note: The site is about 35 km north of Aix-en-Provence.
